text: The study evaluated frozen local corpora where every answer had to be produced within ten tool calls and a laptop-friendly latency budget.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: Researchers compared lexical retrieval, dense retrieval, and a merged hybrid stage over the same 132 chunk corpus pack.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: Hybrid lexical plus dense retrieval raised answer recall by 14 points over lexical-only search on multi-hop questions.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: Precision recovered only when a reranker cut the merged candidate pool from 24 chunks down to 6 chunks before synthesis.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: Dense-only retrieval regularly missed exact method names and section labels that were easy for lexical search to recover.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: The paper recommends keeping lexical search in the first stage, merging a small dense pool, and reranking before drafting.
title: Hybrid Retrieval Under Tight Tool Budgets

text: This benchmark focused on comparison questions that required method evidence, tradeoffs, and limitations from separate sources.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: A decomposition planner generated subqueries for method, evidence, limitation, and constraint handling before retrieval.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: Decomposing comparison prompts raised evidence coverage from 0.41 to 0.73 because the system stopped collapsing every need into one search string.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: The extra subqueries only paid off when the stop rule terminated after marginal gains flattened across the evidence groups.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: Naive decomposition without a stop rule wasted tool calls and repeated near-duplicate chunks.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: Use targeted subqueries for evidence groups, then stop once method, limitation, and comparison evidence are all covered.
title: Query Decomposition For Comparison Tasks

text: A long-horizon autoresearch run compared carrying the full transcript against writing structured memory after each round.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: The structured memory template stored tried queries, failed evidence paths, useful source ids, and open gaps for the next round.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: Compressed memory preserved answer quality while cutting prompt footprint by 38 percent relative to transcript carryover.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: Runs with explicit anti-pattern notes avoided repeating dead-end queries in later rounds.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: Transcript carryover caused later rounds to anchor on stale failed hypotheses and to over-repeat earlier wording.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: Keep a compact memory that records winning evidence, failed branches, and unresolved gaps instead of replaying the whole session.
title: Memory Compression Beats Full Transcript Carryover

text: This evaluation measured how different stop rules behaved when retrieval and synthesis were bounded by visible budgets.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: The strongest variant tracked whether each new tool call added a new evidence group or a previously unseen supporting chunk.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: A marginal gain stop rule improved average score because it halted once new searches stopped expanding evidence coverage.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: Simple fixed-depth loops either stopped too early on hard tasks or burned budget on repetitive searches.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: Counting raw search hits as progress created false confidence even when the hits repeated the same claim.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: Stop when new calls stop adding evidence groups, new source diversity, or novel support chunks.
title: Marginal Gain Stop Rules For Research Loops

text: The spec defines citation validity for a benchmark where every cited chunk must exist and support the relevant claim.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: Valid citations were measured against known support chunk sets rather than against an open-ended semantic verifier.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: Strict overlap with predeclared support chunks made scoring faster and more reproducible than freeform citation judging.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: The benchmark only needed the judge model for synthesis nuance after rule-based citation checks had already run.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: Loose citation grading let polished answers cite nearby but unsupported chunks and still earn inflated scores.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: Use fixed support chunk sets for citation validity and reserve model judges for narrow synthesis disputes.
title: Strict Citation Checks For Frozen Corpus Benchmarks

text: Researchers compared pure LLM judging against a hybrid scorer with hidden answer facets, contradictions, and evidence groups.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: Both systems scored the same research briefs, but only the hybrid scorer had access to hidden facet checklists and forbidden claims.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: Facet-first scoring reduced variance and produced more defensible decisions on short evidence-backed briefs.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: Judge-only scoring drifted on borderline paraphrases and often rewarded style over factual coverage.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: Without hidden contradictions, the judge occasionally passed answers that blended correct facts with subtle but important errors.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: Make hidden facets and contradiction checks primary, then use a fixed judge only as a narrow synthesis layer.
title: Facet-First Evaluation Beats Judge-Only Scoring

text: This report analyzed what happens when the corpus includes both supporting and limiting evidence for the same claim.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: The system logged supportive evidence, limiting evidence, and unresolved conflicts in separate evidence buckets.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: Answers were more trustworthy when the final brief named the strongest support and the main limitation instead of forcing a single-sided conclusion.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: Contradiction buckets helped the system avoid citing a limitation chunk as if it were supportive evidence.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: Naive majority voting collapsed nuance and erased important caveats from minority but credible sources.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: Track support and limitation evidence separately, then surface both when claims remain contested.
title: Contradiction Handling Through Evidence Buckets

text: The study tested whether smaller or larger chunks worked better for brief generation and citation checks.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: Chunk sizes ranged from single paragraphs up to multi-section windows with overlapping stride.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: Mid-sized chunks preserved enough local context for citation checks without burying support under unrelated text.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: Very large chunks improved recall but weakened citation precision because support and caveats were mixed together.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: Single-sentence chunks fragmented methodology descriptions and forced too many retrieval calls.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: Use paragraph-scale chunks with stable section metadata when citation validity matters.
title: Chunk Granularity And Citation Reliability

text: This analysis asked whether better briefs cited more chunks or simply more diverse sources.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: Coverage was decomposed into source diversity, evidence type diversity, and repeated support from the same source.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: Source diversity predicted robust answers better than raw chunk count because multiple sources reduced single-document overfitting.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: The best systems usually cited at least one method source and one limitation or tradeoff source.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: Repeatedly citing the same source looked thorough but left important failure evidence undiscovered.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: Track source diversity explicitly and prefer citations that span method, result, and limitation evidence.
title: Source Diversity As A Coverage Signal

text: The benchmark compared blind retry loops against a critique step that diagnosed why the previous brief missed evidence.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: After each draft, the critique step asked which facet was missing, which citation was weak, and what retrieval gap remained.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: Critique-guided retries improved final score because each new round targeted a missing facet or unsupported claim.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: Blind retries consumed comparable tokens but mostly paraphrased the same weak evidence.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: Retry policies without explicit failure diagnosis repeated the first retrieval query and citation set.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: Use critique to name the missing facet or weak citation before starting another retrieval round.
title: Critique Loops Beat Blind Retries

text: This study examined when query expansion helps or hurts in a benchmark with hard call and token budgets.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: The strongest strategy expanded only one or two key terms with synonyms tied to task type and then reranked aggressively.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: Limited query expansion improved recall on methodology and comparison tasks without breaking the budget.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: Unbounded synonym expansion inflated candidate pools and pushed the system into budget penalties.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: Expansion on every noun phrase created many near-duplicate results and left no room for verification calls.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: Expand only the high-value terms, keep the pool small, and preserve budget for reranking and verification.
title: Budget-Aware Query Expansion

text: A reranking ablation tested whether chunk metadata about evidence type improved brief quality.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: Chunks carried section tags such as method, result, limitation, and recommendation during reranking.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: Evidence-type tags helped the reranker surface one result chunk and one limitation chunk for balanced answers.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: Metadata-aware reranking outperformed text-only ranking on tasks that required tradeoff discussion.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: Text-only reranking over-selected result sections and skipped the limitation evidence needed for strong coverage.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: Keep section and evidence-type metadata in the index and let reranking use it explicitly.
title: Evidence-Type Tags Help Rerankers

text: This report focused on which run artifacts actually helped teams improve their scaffold between evaluations.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: Runs emitted raw outputs, per-task score breakdowns, query traces, and explicit failure labels.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: Teams improved faster when they could see whether a miss came from retrieval, citation validity, or synthesis coverage.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: Per-task score breakdowns made it obvious whether the next change should target evidence coverage or unsupported claims.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: Single scalar scores without artifacts encouraged random tweaking because users could not see why a run failed.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: Store raw outputs and component scores for every task so contestants can debug specific failure modes.
title: Logging Failure Modes For Faster Iteration

text: A controlled benchmark asked systems to choose the best method under explicit latency, cost, or evidence constraints.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: Methods with the highest unconstrained accuracy were not always optimal once runtime and tool limits were applied.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: Constraint-aware selection worked best when the answer explicitly named the winning method and the reason it fit the constraint.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: High-accuracy but slow methods often lost under strict wall-clock or tool-call caps.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: Drafts that ignored the stated constraint were judged wrong even when their unconstrained recommendation sounded strong.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: For selection tasks, align the answer to the named constraint before optimizing for absolute accuracy.
title: Constraint-Aware Selection Beats Max-Accuracy Drafting

text: The evaluation design grouped hidden evidence into method, support, limitation, and recommendation buckets.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: A task only earned full coverage when its citations spanned all required evidence groups.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: Evidence groups stopped shallow systems from winning with one strong quote that ignored the rest of the verification path.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: Group-aware scoring especially improved multi-hop comparison tasks where method and limitation evidence lived in different chunks.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: Without evidence groups, answers with narrow but eloquent support scored too well.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: Define hidden evidence groups per task and require coverage across them, not just one valid citation.
title: Evidence Groups Make Multi-Hop Tasks Defensible

text: This retrieval study emphasized that titles, sections, and source metadata often carry the exact discriminators a benchmark needs.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: The system indexed source title tokens, section labels, and year metadata alongside chunk text.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: Metadata-first retrieval rescued tasks that asked for methodology or limitation evidence because those cues were often in headers.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: Plain text search missed important chunks when the body used pronouns but the header named the relevant method directly.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: Ignoring metadata made many retrieval misses look mysterious even though the answer cue was sitting in the title field.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: Index titles and sections as first-class search features rather than treating metadata as decoration.
title: Metadata-First Retrieval For Frozen Corpora

text: A note-taking ablation asked whether lightweight note tools help under small budgets.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: The tool only allowed concise notes that recorded which claim a chunk supported and which gap still remained.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: Short notes improved verification because the system could remember why a citation was chosen without rereading every chunk.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: The gain was strongest when notes were claim-linked instead of generic summaries.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: Verbose note dumps consumed tokens and duplicated chunk text instead of sharpening the next action.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: Use notes sparingly to link claims, citations, and remaining gaps rather than to restate the corpus.
title: Short Notes Help Verification Calls

text: The benchmark compared short evidence-backed briefs against long reasoning traces for the same tasks.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps

text: Both variants had access to the same retrieval stack, but one had to answer in a compact structured brief.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps

text: Concise briefs scored better because they were easier to validate against hidden facets and citation rules.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps

text: Long reasoning dumps increased the chance of unsupported side claims and contradiction penalties.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps

text: Verbose answers often wandered beyond the retrieved evidence and mixed speculation with supported findings.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps

text: Require short structured briefs with citations, and avoid long chain-of-thought style outputs.
title: Concise Synthesis Outperforms Long Reasoning Dumps
